_doc: The ONE registry of actions the read-only ✦ chat may offer as buttons. Both sides read this file: srv/prompts.py teaches Claude the menu from it, and src/chatActions.ts dispatches a clicked button from it — so the taught vocabulary and the wired dispatch can never drift. The chat itself stays read-only (Read/Grep/Glob); an action is a PROPOSAL the viewer renders and the human clicks to run against an endpoint that already exists.

actions.label: Set branch purpose
actions.describe: Save a one-line purpose as this branch's git description. Offer it when you can state, in plain language, what the branch is for.

params.name: text
params.desc: the one-line purpose in plain language — what the branch does, not how it's coded

actions.label: Bless this file
actions.describe: Mark the file under review as blessed. Offer it only in a file-scoped chat when the file's change looks correct and complete.

actions.label: Squash to working tree
actions.describe: Collapse the branch's parent..branch history into unstaged working-tree changes (Phil writes the commit himself). Offer when the branch has messy WIP commits worth flattening.

actions.label: Prep to merge
actions.describe: Squash the whole branch into one clean, formatted commit for a single-commit PR. Offer when the branch is ready to ship.

actions.label: Restack onto origin/main
actions.describe: Rebase this unpublished root branch onto fresh origin/main. Offer when the branch has fallen behind main.

actions.label: Apply this change
actions.describe: Hand a specific, concrete edit to a full (editing) Claude running in the branch's worktree — this is how a read-only suggestion gets executed. Offer only in a file-scoped chat, and only when you can state the exact change as a precise instruction.

params.name: instruction
params.desc: a precise, self-contained instruction describing the edit to make to this file
